survey: A wooden pier shown from a high three-quarter front view, running away from the viewer toward a horizon set high in the frame. Two thick front posts stand at the waterline on wet sand. Each sits in foam with flat elliptical ripples, and both top faces are seen from above as ellipses. The left post has a coil of rope wrapped around it, and its loops are ellipses that match the post's top. The right post holds a metal hook, and a red-and-white lifebuoy hangs from it on a rope, almost face-on, in front of the post and to its right. A front beam with two bolts runs between the posts. It is nearly level and drops slightly to the right, which matches the right post standing a little lower and closer. Behind the beam, the plank deck runs back. The planks run across the pier and get thinner and closer together with distance. Their left ends step inward and the deck's side edges come together toward a single point beyond the far end. Small brackets and a middle support post sit under the deck in the water. Four back posts rise above the far end of the deck. They are smaller and their top faces are thinner ellipses than the front posts' tops, which fits their nearness to the horizon. The far-right post meets the water higher in the frame, as distance requires. The camera height, the flat water, the deck top and every post top agree on one viewpoint.
